newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wienerberger 96 pretax profit down 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wienerberger 96 pretax profit down 13 pct.

text.p: Austria's Wienerberger Baustoffindustrie AG, the world's largest brickmaker, said on Thursday preliminary pretax profit last year fell 13 percent to 1.3 billion schillings.
Wienerberger, however, said it expected pretax profit this year to rise 25 percent.
"The prevailing weak building volume in Europe was aggravated by the extremely long and severe winter," the company said in a statement.
"Due to marked price declines in Austria and Germany our traditionally most profitable division, bricks, experienced substantially reduced profitability," it continued.
In the brick division, pretax profit tumbled to 650 million schillings from 882 million.
The company said the pretax profit of 1.3 billion schillings was in line with its expectations of between 1.2 to 1.4 billion after 1.5 billion in 1995.
In October, Wienerberger's chief executive Erhard Schaschl said he expected the group to turn in a pretax profit of 1.4 billion schillings for 1996.
Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) slipped to 1.66 billion schillings from 1.674 billion in 1995.
Group sales climbed to 14.6 billion from 12.9 billion in 1995 and operating profit was largely unchanged at 1.7 billion.

The company said its acquisition of Belgium's largest brickmaker Terca Bricks was a decisive factor in strengthening its performance, with Terca contributing 325 million schillings to the group's pretax profit.
Terca contributed sales worth 2.4 billion schillings to the group total. Wienerberger bought Terca last April.
The company said it was optimistic for the current year, seeing sales increase 10 percent and pretax profit jumping 25 percent.
"At the same time, we are planning to continue our expansion in 1997 -- on top of our industrial presence which comprises already 152 plants in 21 countries," it said.
